access_policy: Access is an explicit reviewer judgment in each active card. A cached PDF is not automatically a full-text reading. Full text means relevant sections inspected.

active_bibliography_rows.finding: Exists and supports a causal-response-model fidelity obstruction; full text not obtained. Avoid extending the abstract's language to every dielectric architecture.
Continuous-time XPM response and phase-noise model; probe/parity-gate analysis is not an architecture-independent phase maximum.
Local multimode interaction and bandwidth/fidelity tradeoff; stated assumptions matter.
Analytical high-fidelity conditional phase in a nonlocal, chi(2)-equivalent model with unequal velocities; not a counterexample inside strict local bulk Kerr.
Discrete atom-mediated counter-propagating architecture; fidelity allows specified single-photon distortion corrections. Not a transparent-bulk material bound.
Memory citation verified. Strong classical controls change cavity coupling; storage and incident pulse duration are independent resources. This is outside a passive time-independent architecture.
Emitter/cavity photon-transport gate; does not establish a bound for transparent bulk chi(3).
Index bound has dispersion/bandwidth conditions; no automatic nonlinear extension.
Original source and correction metadata located. Molecular hyperpolarizability, not a universal bulk Kerr theorem.
Truncation/ansatz assumptions are part of the theory, not consequences of macroscopic transparency alone.
Main calculation concerns second-order molecular response; third-order response is proposed as subsequent work.
Omitted direct third-order molecular bound. Full corrected derivation remains to be checked.
Few-level ansatz and formal many-state catastrophe; does not prove a physically attainable bulk divergence.

active_bibliography_rows.source: Shim, Fan, Johnson and Miller, DOI [10.1103/PhysRevX.9.011043](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.9.011043)
active_bibliography_rows.finding: Vague memory citation resolved. Bandwidth-averaged response/LDOS limits do not directly bound the internal energy-normalized quartic interaction.
Article year is **2018**, despite the DOI's 2017 string. Fiber XPM metrology with mixed probes/postselection; not a demonstrated high-fidelity two-photon gate.
Memory citation verified. Self-similar dielectric concentration is feature-size sensitive; peak-energy mode volume differs from nonlinear interaction volume.
Review located; covers resonant platforms outside the strict bulk-transparent class as well as general quantum nonlinear optics.
Vague Mabuchi-group lead resolved: auxiliary trap pulse and dispersion engineering; demonstrated model uses chi(2)-mediated gate dynamics. Additional control resources must be counted.
Resonant quantum-well second/third-order bounds, not the proposed general off-resonant bulk Kerr limit.
Clarifies nonlinear analyticity and signed sum-rule strengths; closes a logical shortcut in the proposed combination.
Fabrication-constrained mode-volume bounds already exist, including multiple resonances; their point-energy objective does not itself bound a gate channel.

Current tutorial explicitly leaves general bandwidth-dependent nonlinear material bounds open and reviews regularized mode-volume limits. This supports the narrower material subquestion, not the original combined gate ceiling.

active_bibliography_rows.source: C. L. Epstein, minimum-energy pulse synthesis, DOI [10.1016/j.jmr.2003.12.014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmr.2003.12.014)
active_bibliography_rows.finding: Minimum-energy inverse-scattering result is real; full author PDF was blocked. Do not attribute its exact normalization from the abstract.
Sole author, not “Epstein & Magland”; theorem supplies the exact trace identity and bound-state penalty.
Log-transmittance area for a different, counter-propagating stack model; useful analogy, not this optimization problem.
Located current preprint; wavelength-integrated mirror bound has different assumptions and integration weight.
Located paper and abstract in a copy of the original article; metal-backed absorber bound, not an SFG theorem.
Linear slow-light limit; no nonlinear-conversion conclusion inferred.
The area law is derived in the weak-conversion limit and explicitly ceases to hold at saturation; original author list was inaccurate.

active_bibliography_rows.source: Suchowski, Oron, Arie and Silberberg, [arXiv:0805.1517](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1517), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevA.78.063821
active_bibliography_rows.finding: SFG/Bloch mapping and adiabatic QPM designs precede this card.
Fully nonlinear adiabatic conditions **and a bandwidth estimate** already exist; they are not an all-poling trace bound.
Cascaded adiabatic conversion, not a global optimum over the present controls.
Composite-crystal designs include depleted and undepleted operation; this is a stronger precedent than the original listing conveyed.
Frequency-domain WKB design formulas for chirped OPA; exact coefficients and edge corrections not independently audited here.
Apodization paper exists; coauthor is **L. Gallmann**, not L. Lin.
Numerical optimal-control studies constrain amplitude and RF power separately; do not interpret their numerical limits as a global impossibility theorem.
Ensemble control is established; admissible controls differ from binary QPM.
The previously vague lead is located: inverse scattering of corrugated filters.
Located institutional abstract: exact differential layer-peeling synthesis of fiber Bragg gratings; no new conversion theorem attributed to it.
Omitted close precedent: inverse synthesis of **codirectional** coupling spectra.
Necessary/sufficient realizability constraints and inverse synthesis are already claimed for a discrete coupler model. Full text needed before claiming novelty for an unconstrained reachable set.

Omitted binary-grating precedent: inverse scattering plus a transfer-matrix genetic optimization, including corrections to the effective-envelope approximation. An achieved flat-band design is not a certified global bandwidth frontier.
Omitted close precedent: convex QPM design under stated linear/first-order-QPM approximations, including fabrication constraints. Does not establish the exact high-conversion binary frontier.

Main article supplies analytical minimum-energy and bounded-amplitude bang–bang designs through a spin–spring projection with an additional feasibility condition. The supplement's control optimization remains to be audited; do not equate it with a worst-band-error frontier under minimum-domain constraints.
First initial corrected; soliton efficiency scaling, with a pulse-energy convention that needs care when comparing pump-excluded power.

active_bibliography_rows.source: **X. Xue, P.-H. Wang, Y. Xuan, M. Qi and A. M. Weiner**, DOI [10.1002/lpor.201600276](https://doi.org/10.1002/lpor.201600276), arXiv:1610.00958
active_bibliography_rows.finding: Original author list corrected; effective critical coupling is a general energy-flow argument, not merely a duty-cycle fit.
Single-soliton scaling regimes; no all-state conclusion inferred from the abstract.
Coupled-cavity pump matching; different system from the uniform single-ring problem.
Coupled-ring efficiency enhancement verified; full supplementary derivation was not independently read here.
Soliton-ansatz optimization; paper discusses disagreement with simulations at low normalized drive. Its formal unity limit is not a certified exact stationary-state optimum.

active_bibliography_rows.source: **J. Gärtner** et al., DOI [10.1103/PhysRevA.100.033819](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.100.033819); author preprint DOI 10.5445/IR/1000089036
active_bibliography_rows.finding: First initial corrected; numerical bifurcation/continuation and the external-power normalization are established.
First initials corrected; dark-pulse approximation has the squared-coupling maximum. Review's definition can include pump power under the comb envelope, unlike strict pump-line exclusion here.
Their dual-pump metric includes weighted contributions **from both pump modes**. Its weak-drive limit is not a limit on new-line conversion. See registered algebra check.
A priori estimates and bifurcations constrain possible branches but do not solve the requested conversion frontier.

active_bibliography_rows.source: Gasmi, Jahnke, Kirn and Reichel, [arXiv:2210.09779](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.09779), DOI 10.1007/s00033-023-02060-3
active_bibliography_rows.finding: Existence, uniqueness and continuation results for dual pumping; relevant theorems inspected, but no conversion-efficiency optimization supplied.
Platicon demonstration; coupling calibration not independently reconstructed.
Initial corrected; bidirectional system needs its own port and power bookkeeping.
Resonant chi(2) efficiency/critical-coupling theory already exists; comb allocation beyond that model is a different question.
Mean-field chi(2) comb model, not a global conversion optimizer.
Previously unaccessed normalization/model reference located in an author PDF.
Previously unlocated lead verified: three-mode OPO optimum and multimode competing processes. Not a solution of the all-branch LLE problem.
OPO signal/idler coupling-product ceiling stated explicitly; track photon versus power efficiency.
Earlier triply resonant Kerr-OPO optimization with loss and couplings; rules out novelty for an undifferentiated “more ports” ceiling.
Explicit internal ceiling and external-coupling relation, missed by proposer.

active_bibliography_rows.source: Reddy, Raymer, McKinstrie, Mejling and Rottwitt, [arXiv:1305.2165](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.2165), DOI 10.1364/OE.21.013840
active_bibliography_rows.finding: Exact matched-regime Green function and numerical parameter exploration; pump chirp can be removed from the Schmidt spectrum in that regime. This is not a proof over every velocity configuration.
Omitted erratum corrects time arguments in the original Green-function equations; conclusions stated unchanged. Use corrected expressions in an oracle.
Temporal-mode interferometry is a cascaded architecture, outside the proposed single-pass class.
Multistage theory and numerical high selectivity; no all-pump single-stage proof found.
Explicitly describes the single-stage limit as obtained by exhaustive numerical exploration.
Mode-selective conversion, time ordering and cascade scaling; finite-order analysis is not a global ceiling proof.
Magnus formalism supporting the mechanism; retain its approximation assumptions.

active_bibliography_rows.source: Christ, Brecht, Mauerer and Silberhorn, [arXiv:1210.8342](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8342), DOI 10.1088/1367-2630/15/5/053038
active_bibliography_rows.finding: Rigorous numerical propagation versus neglect of time ordering; explicitly leaves perfect engineered single-mode high-gain conversion open.

active_bibliography_rows.source: Brecht, Reddy, Silberhorn and Raymer, DOI [10.1103/PhysRevX.5.041017](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.5.041017)
active_bibliography_rows.finding: Review of temporal modes; numerical ceiling, not a new theorem.

active_bibliography_rows.source: Ansari, Donohue, Brecht and Silberhorn, DOI [10.1364/OPTICA.5.000534](https://doi.org/10.1364/OPTICA.5.000534)
active_bibliography_rows.finding: Review of temporal-mode engineering and architectures; no global proof found in the relevant conversion discussion.
Dichroic-cavity selection uses a different Green operator.

First author is Silia Babel, not L. Babel. Selectivity is a normalized mode fraction measured in a finite test basis with output filtering at low pump power; high conversion is measured separately. It is not a demonstrated violation of the Reddy $S$ ceiling.
The percentage highlighted by the original card refers to conversion efficiency, not a global selectivity bound.
Omitted experimental temporal-mode interferometry precedent; an architecture comparison, not a single-pass counterexample.
Earlier Green-function/Schmidt treatment of frequency translation in fiber; mathematical framework itself is established.

Efficiency–mode-discrimination tradeoffs and a genuine Slepian reduction for sequential rectangular time/frequency filters. That filter kernel is different from the nonlinear single-pass Bessel kernel; its bound cannot be imported without proving an equivalence.
Driven-power upper bound, with undepleted pump and explicit norm/discretization relaxation; not a normalized eigenmode bound.
Review's outlook identifies nonlinear and eigenproblem objectives as limitations of the then quadratic framework; no requested overlap theorem found there.
Appendix F inspected: nonlinear power-conservation formulation and possible bounds, not the requested closed modal-overlap ceiling.
Original A. M. initial wrong; separated-region quartic bound and singularity discussion are essential to interpretation.
Depleted two-mode conversion theory already established.
Nonlinear-overlap optimization gives achievable designs, not certified global maxima; comparison requires identical normalization/design class.
Located original molecular bound and correction metadata; not a bulk or structural theorem.
Frequency-dependent molecular hyperpolarizability treatment using the few-level ansatz, not a Maxwell shape bound.
Causality/sum-rule identities do not alone supply a positive structural optimization bound.
Extended-system second-order response bound depends on band gap, bandwidth and microscopic geometry; not obtained by naive molecular-density scaling.
Resonant quantum-well susceptibilities, not all transparent bulk materials or all cavity shapes.
Nonlinear oscillator strengths need not be positive; sum rules are constraints, not automatically an extremal theorem.
Original D. Wang wrong; nonlinear critical coupling and device demonstration, not an all-geometry bound.
Relevant omitted geometric warning: dielectric field concentration depends on fabrication scale; pointwise mode volume and nonlinear overlap are distinct.
Omitted close precedent: computational mode-volume bounds with minimum features and simultaneous resonances; does not optimize the nonlinear overlap.

Current tutorial separates nonlinear material bounds, sharp-tip concentration and minimum physical size; its citations led to the Zhao multiresonance result. Only these relevant sections were audited.
